title: Birth of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
description: Born as Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar in Mhow, Central Provinces (now Madhya Pradesh), to Ramji Maloji Sakpal and Bhimabai. He was the 14th child of the family.

title: Early Schooling — Satara
description: Family moved to Satara after father's transfer. Young Bhim attended local school, facing caste-based discrimination early in life.

title: Father Retired — Move to Bombay
description: Ramji Sakpal retired from military service. Family shifted to Bombay (now Mumbai). Bhim enrolled at Elphinstone High School.

title: Matriculation — Elphinstone High School
description: Bhimrao passed matriculation from Elphinstone High School, Bombay. He was the first from his Mahar community to do so. Celebrated in his community.

title: Enrolled at Elphinstone College
description: Joined Elphinstone College, affiliated with University of Bombay. Studied Economics and Political Science.

title: Graduation — B.A. in Economics & Political Science
description: Graduated from Elphinstone College with a B.A. degree. His success was celebrated across the Mahar community. The degree was conferred by Bombay University.

title: Scholarship to Columbia University
description: Secured the Baroda State Scholarship for study in New York. Left for Columbia University to pursue graduate studies in Economics and Political Science.

title: M.A. — Columbia University
description: Completed M.A. in Economics at Columbia University. Specialized in Economics, Sociology, History, Philosophy and Anthropology. Thesis: 'Ancient Indian Commerce'.

title: D.Sc. — London School of Economics
description: Enrolled at the London School of Economics. Began work on doctoral thesis. Also studied at Gray's Inn for law.

title: D.Sc. in Economics — London School of Economics
description: Completed his second doctorate — D.Sc. in Economics from LSE. His thesis 'The Problem of the Rupee' examined currency systems and gold exchange standards.

title: Called to the Bar — Gray's Inn
description: Qualified as a barrister-at-law from Gray's Inn, London. Returned to India in 1923 with multiple advanced degrees — an extraordinary achievement for someone from his community.

title: Started Legal Practice in Bombay
description: Established his legal practice in Bombay High Court. Also taught at the prestigious Sydenham College of Commerce.

title: Appointed to Bombay University Senate
description: Nominated to the Senate of Bombay University. Began working on social reform for the depressed classes.

title: Called for Separate Electorates — Simon Commission
description: Appeared before the Simon Commission and demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes. This became a key point in constitutional negotiations.

title: Round Table Conference — First
description: Participated in the First Round Table Conference in London as a representative of the Depressed Classes. Demanded separate electorates for untouchables.

title: Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi
description: Negotiated the Poona Pact with Gandhi at Yerwada Jail. Abandoned separate electorates in exchange for 18% reservation for Depressed Classes in legislatures.

title: Second Round Table Conference
description: Participated in the Second Round Table Conference. Continued advocacy for Depressed Classes rights.

title: Published 'Annihilation of Caste'
description: Published his seminal work 'Annihilation of Caste' — an undelivered speech written for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal (Lahore). Became his most famous work.

title: Government of India Act, 1935
description: The Government of India Act incorporated provisions Ambedkar had advocated for, including reserved seats for Depressed Classes.

title: Founded Independent Labour Party
description: Founded the Independent Labour Party (ILP) in Bombay. The party contested elections and won several seats.

title: Annihilation of Caste Published
description: Self-published after organizers cancelled the speech. Over 15,000 copies sold. Considered the most powerful critique of caste ever written.

title: Bombay Legislative Council — Elected Member
description: Elected to the Bombay Legislative Council as an ILP candidate. Became Leader of the Opposition.

title: Appointed to Viceroy's Executive Council
description: Nominated as Labour Member. Worked on labor rights, minimum wages, and working conditions for industrial workers.

title: Elected to Constituent Assembly
description: Elected to the Constituent Assembly of India as representative of the Depressed Classes. Would become chief architect of the Constitution.

title: First Law Minister of India
description: Appointed as the first Law Minister of independent India. Also served as Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

title: Draft Constitution Completed
description: The Draft Constitution was completed after 2 years, 11 months, and 17 days of work. Contained 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.

title: Constitution Adopted
description: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949. Ambedkar moved the motion: 'The Constitution is passed.'

title: Resigned from Cabinet
description: Resigned from Nehru's cabinet over disagreement on the Hindu Code Bill and other policy matters.

title: Elected to Lok Sabha — Bombay North
description: Contested the first general election from Bombay North and won. Became a member of the First Lok Sabha.

title: Published 'Buddha and His Dhamma'
description: Published his final major work. Presents Buddhism as a rational, scientific philosophy. Completed shortly before his own conversion.

title: Conversion to Buddhism — Nagpur
description: Formally embraced Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur, along with approximately 500,000 followers — the largest mass conversion in history.

title: Passing of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
description: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar passed away in his sleep at his Delhi residence. He was 65. Cremated at Dadar Chowpatty, Mumbai, per Buddhist rites.
